newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CITIC says China telco mkts need two bln yuan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CITIC says China telco mkts need two bln yuan.

text.p: MELBOURNE, Dec 2 (REUTER) - China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC) would need to invest a total of about two billion yuan in its four Chinese telecommunications markets in order to break even, president Qin Xiao said on Monday.

"The first stage would be four cities. I think the break-even point for each city would be about 150,000 customers and that takes something like 500 million Chinese yuan (per city)," Xiao told a small press briefing.

Xiao, who is in Australia for an international trade conference targeted primarily at boosting trade with Asia, said the group's telecommunications strategy in China centred on the cities of Tianjin, Xian, Wuhan and Shenyang.

CITIC holds a telecommunications licence in the cities by virtue of its investment along with seven other Chinese companies in China's state-run telecommunications competitor China United Telecommunications (Unicom).

Xiao said the group's view of how long it would take to reach breakeven point had been clouded by friction between CITIC and the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, who's China Telecom dominates wireless communications in the country.

"Because there are some friction and fighting between (CITIC and the Ministry), in the very beginning we thought it would take a couple of years, now we believe it will be a little bit longer," he said.
CITIC's initial focus in the Chinese telecommunications market was on cellular mobile telephones, but the difficulty lay in combating cheaper cellular services offered by China Telecom.
"Because they have other interests in fixed (land) lines, they can reduce the price for cellular phone it makes (it) difficult for survival."
Xiao was, nonetheless, bullish about the prospects for Chinese telecommunication companies.
"If you single out one sector which stands as the biggest market in China, that's telecommunications. The market is huge, particularly in the countryside" Xiao said.
China had 6.2 million mobile phone users at the end of October and the market in cellular communications was expected to further boom next year, the official Xinhua news agency said last month.
Xiao said the second stage of CITIC's thrust into the telecoms market was to set up land lines but he gave no further details.
